name: Heavy Chain Deposition Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Heavy Chain Deposition Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Renal biopsy showing linear deposition of monoclonal heavy chains along glomerular and tubular basement membranes by immunofluorescence
Detection of monoclonal heavy chain protein in serum or urine by immunofixation electrophoresis
Exclusion of light chain deposition disease by immunofluorescence and electron microscopy
Presence of proteinuria and/or renal insufficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of renal biopsy confirming heavy chain deposition plus detection of monoclonal heavy chain protein in serum or urine, with exclusion of light chain deposition disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on renal biopsy and immunofluorescence studies; electron microscopy supports diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal heavy chain deposition in renal basement membranes

laboratory: Monoclonal heavy chain detected by serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or increased echogenicity
Skeletal survey may show lytic lesions if associated plasma cell dyscrasia present
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; associated with plasma cell clone producing truncated heavy chains
other: Renal biopsy with immunofluorescence demonstrating linear heavy chain deposits
Electron microscopy showing punctate electron-dense deposits along basement membranes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of monoclonal light chain deposits instead of heavy chains
Amyloid fibril deposits with Congo red positivity and apple-green birefringence
Different ultrastructural appearance on electron microscopy

redFlags: Presence of monoclonal protein in serum or urine
references: Pozzi C, D'Amico M, Fogazzi GB, et al. Heavy chain deposition disease: clinical and pathologic study of 13 patients. Medicine (Baltimore). 1997;76(3):147-157.
